extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and disciplinary counsel handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 when a patent practitioner is disciplined by another duly constituted authority of the United States, including required findings, the discipline imposed, probation conditions, publication, and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose discipline identical to that imposed by a duly constituted authority of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline when a practitioner has been disciplined by another jurisdiction; the Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the statutory/regulatory basis for such action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline is predicated upon the respondent being suspended, stayed, and placed on probation by a duly constituted authority of the United States, resulting in a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO's reciprocal discipline is justified where the practitioner's out-of-Office suspension/probation constitutes a violation of the USPTO disciplinary rule framed in §11.804(h) (i.e., disciplinary action by another jurisdiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent concedes that identical discipline would be appropriate (or otherwise fails to raise a genuine issue of material fact), the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedurally, a timely response is considered and if respondent admits appropriateness of identical discipline, the USPTO can find no genuine factual dispute and adopt the state/court discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' to the respondent (here, sent by certified mail), and the respondent is afforded an opportunity to file a timely response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt no. cited) and delivered; respondent filed a timely response on April 3, 2018. This demonstrates required procedural notice and chance to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition: suspension with stay
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may be suspended from practice before the USPTO for a specified period (here, thirty days) with the period stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order language: 'suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office ... for thirty days, with the period of suspension stayed.' Specifies scope (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters) and commencement tied to the Final Order date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation term and general probation condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may be placed on probation for a specified period (here, three years) during which specific conditions must be satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order: 'be placed on probation for three years, commencing on the date of this Final Order, during which respondent must ...' Probation term is tied to the Final Order date and includes enumerated mandatory conditions (see separate entry for those six items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated probation conditions (six required items)
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation respondent must: (1) not commit any other violation of the D.C. Rules of Professional Conduct or disciplinary rules of any other jurisdiction (excluding reciprocal discipline for these violations); (2) remain in individual therapy with his treating psychologist; (3) attend Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) at least two times a week and submit proof of attendance to his psychologist; (4) continue use of psychotropic medication as prescribed by psychiatrist and meet with psychiatrist every three months; (5) execute and maintain waivers/consent forms to permit psychologist and psychiatrist to contact the D.C. Bar Lawyer Assistance Program (LAP) if respondent ceases treatment or fails to attend AA; and (6) authorize LAP to report to Disciplinary Counsel if respondent stops treatment, fails to attend AA, or revokes consent preventing LAP from reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These substantive, behavioral, and monitoring conditions are imposed as part of probation. The Order repeats these six items verbatim and makes authorization/waiver requirements a condition allowing third-party reporting to disciplinary authorities for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of stayed suspension and probation notice in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the specified template notice describing the stayed suspension, probation, grounds, and probation conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice template in the Order includes: respondent identity and registration number, summary of discipline (thirty-day stayed suspension and three-year probation), citation to violated rule (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), summary factual basis (conduct regarding representation of two joint clients), enumerated probation conditions, and reference to OED FOIA Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory notification obligation to ensure other jurisdictions and courts are informed of USPTO discipline; the Order directs OED to provide such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual basis / misconduct findings (D.C. Rules cited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The District of Columbia Court of Appeals found respondent's misconduct arose from representation of two joint clients and included failures such as depositing client-paid funds into an operating account and not paying filing fees; respondent acknowledged violations of D.C. Rules 1.1(a) and (b), 1.3(a), 1.4(a), and 1.15(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order details the underlying factual misconduct (failure to file paid-for applications, poor communication, commingling client funds) and cites specific Rules of Professional Conduct violated: competence (1.1(a),(b)), diligence (1.3(a)), communication (1.4(a)), and safekeeping of client property/commingling (1.15(a)). These factual findings constitute the basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of disciplinary decisions for public review
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states: 'Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room' and provides the URL. This establishes a transparency/publication practice.
